purpose: Map the current support/coverage/cost tradeoff so the paper reports answer coverage alongside grounded correctness and does not hide improvements caused by abstention.
scope_notes: Aggregate rows use examples 241-389 where direct, risk-gate, and claim-entailment policies share a judged 149-example surface.
Local zero-call scaffold rows use the final 321-389 surface from the DRAG-like comparison and are included as cheap failure-mode anchors.
Historical judge costs are evaluation costs already spent; online_openai_calls_per_query estimates inference-time calls for the policy family.

systems.interpretation: Best judged answer coverage among the current aggregate policies, but lower support.
Improves judged correctness and answer support by abstaining on more rows.
Best zero-extra-call support/correctness operating point, with the lowest answer coverage among the aggregate judged policies.
Highest current correctness estimate, but it uses a per-query mini judge and is therefore not the final amortized zero-call scaffold.
Distilling to a span selector improves coverage over the extractive floor, but judged answer support remains low because selected spans can be topically relevant without answering the question.
Naive local SFT on compact RAG labels can learn to emit cited answers but does not preserve support, showing why the paper needs support-aware joint-action data rather than generic SFT.

conclusions: The current completed support gains are real but mostly buy support by abstaining more.
The claim-entailment guard is the best zero-extra-call support-first operating point among aggregate judged policies.
The mini-verifier gate has stronger correctness but violates the desired low-cost amortization shape because it adds a per-query LLM verifier.
The zero-call local/tiny-model attempts are not yet acceptable substitutes for the missing Qwen 3B joint-action run.
required_next_evidence: Run the Qwen 3B joint-action smoke and place it on this same table.
Judge Qwen 3B predictions for answer support, abstention support, and overall grounded correctness.
Report answer rate and citation recall alongside correctness so abstention-driven gains are visible.
